rationale: Both separate regular-frame and tenth-frame handling and score with a flat rolls list. B is cleaner and more idiomatic. It raises the specific ValueError rather than a bare Exception, with distinct messages for negative and too-many pins. It validates a roll before appending it, so an invalid roll leaves the game state unchanged. Its score loop is a flat three-way if/elif that covers all ten frames uniformly. A appends the roll before validating, so after an exception the frame contains the bad roll and the object is corrupted. It also raises generic Exception everywhere. Its tenth-frame code is cluttered by an awkward tuple assignment with a conditional expression, and its score loop has extra nesting and a separate tenth-frame branch. B is more robust and easier to read.
